distractor_rationales.D: Zero urine output for 4 hours indicates acute kidney injury from hypovolemia.

questions.question_text: A postnatal mother 3 days post-episiotomy repair complains of severe, throbbing perineal pain and swelling. Upon inspection, the midwife notes a tense, tender, bluish hematoma over the suture line. What is the appropriate midwifery action?

choices.text: Reassure her that this is completely normal and requires no action
Notify the physician immediately; small hematomas may be managed conservatively with ice packs and analgesics, while large expanding hematomas require surgical evacuation
Remove all episiotomy sutures immediately without medical consultation
Apply boiling hot water compresses directly to the hematoma

questions.rationale: Perineal hematomas cause severe pain. Small ones resolve with ice and analgesia, but large expanding hematomas require surgical drainage and hemostasis.

distractor_rationales.A: Severe throbbing pain and tense hematoma are abnormal pathological complications.
distractor_rationales.C: Removing sutures independently without surgical assessment worsens bleeding.
distractor_rationales.D: Hot compresses worsen bleeding and swelling.

questions.question_text: When performing sterile catheterization or episiotomy care, which technique violates sterile principle guidelines?

choices.text: Opening sterile packages by pulling wrapper flaps away from the center first
Reaching across the sterile field to grab equipment placed on the far side
Holding sterile items above waist level at all times
Treating the outer 1-inch border of a sterile drape as contaminated

questions.rationale: Reaching across a sterile field violates sterile technique because unsterile clothing or arms may inadvertently contaminate the sterile zone.

distractor_rationales.A: Pulling flaps away prevents arms from contaminating sterile contents.
distractor_rationales.C: Holding items above the waist keeps them in view and sterile.
distractor_rationales.D: The outer 1-inch border is universally considered contaminated.

questions.question_text: Which of the following clinical documentation entries demonstrates the most accurate, objective, and legally defensible midwifery assessment note?

choices.text: Client is lazy and uncooperative; refused to take morning antenatal medication.
At 0800, client stated 'my lower belly cramps badly,' uterine contractions present every 4 minutes lasting 45 seconds, FHR 144 bpm.
Client seems fine and is resting comfortably without problems.
Client appears to be exaggerating her labour pain unnecessarily.

questions.rationale: Objective documentation must include direct quotes, measurable vital signs, and observable clinical data without emotional bias or subjective value judgments.

distractor_rationales.A: Using judgmental terms like 'lazy' is unprofessional and legally indefensible.
distractor_rationales.C: Phrases like 'seems fine' are vague and lack objective evidence.
distractor_rationales.D: Accusing a client of exaggerating pain violates professional empathy and objectivity.

questions.question_text: What is the primary physiological reason why pregnant women are more susceptible to peripheral edema in the lower extremities during the third trimester?

choices.text: Increased plasma oncotic pressure and hypervolemia
Increased venous pressure in the lower limbs caused by gravid uterus compression of the inferior vena cava and pelvic veins
Complete cessation of renal filtration function
Severe chronic dehydration

questions.rationale: The enlarging gravid uterus compresses the inferior vena cava and pelvic veins, elevating venous hydrostatic pressure and causing dependent lower extremity edema.

distractor_rationales.A: Plasma oncotic pressure actually decreases slightly in normal pregnancy due to hemodilution.
distractor_rationales.C: Renal filtration rates increase during pregnancy.
distractor_rationales.D: Dehydration reduces fluid retention rather than causes peripheral edema.

questions.question_text: A postnatal mother 5 days post-normal delivery with an episiotomy returns to the clinic complaining of worsening perineal pain, foul-smelling vaginal discharge, and low-grade fever. Upon inspection, the midwife observes wound dehiscence with purulent exudate. What is the appropriate management?

choices.text: Apply tight adhesive bandages over the infected wound
Notify the physician, take wound swab for culture, initiate prescribed antibiotics, perform Sitz baths, and plan secondary closure if indicated
Ignore the infection as episiotomy wounds always heal spontaneously
Instruct the mother to apply herbal sap directly into the open wound

questions.rationale: An infected dehisced episiotomy requires medical notification, wound cultures, antibiotic therapy, local hygiene (Sitz baths), and potential secondary repair.

distractor_rationales.A: Adhesive bandages trap infection and worsen abscess formation.
distractor_rationales.C: Ignoring wound infection leads to necrotizing fasciitis or sepsis.
distractor_rationales.D: Unverified herbal sap causes chemical burns and worsens wound necrosis.

questions.question_text: A midwife is preparing to collect a midstream urine (MSU) specimen for culture and sensitivity from a pregnant woman with suspected urinary tract infection. Which instruction is critical?

choices.text: Collect the very first stream of morning urine directly into the container
Clean perineal area from front to back, pass initial urine stream into toilet, then collect midstream urine in sterile container
Wipe from back to front using standard soap
Refrigerate urine specimen for 48 hours before laboratory submission

questions.rationale: Cleaning front-to-back prevents introducing fecal bacteria, and discarding initial urine flushes out urethral contaminants for accurate culture results.

distractor_rationales.A: Collecting the initial stream captures skin and urethral contaminants.
distractor_rationales.C: Wiping back-to-front transfers E. coli into the urinary meatus.
distractor_rationales.D: Refrigerating for 48 hours alters bacterial growth, invalidating culture results.

questions.question_text: A midwife is assessing four postpartum mothers. Which client requires prioritization for immediate clinical evaluation?

choices.text: A mother 1 day post-delivery breastfeeding successfully with mild afterpains
A mother 2 days post-delivery reporting sudden unilateral calf pain, swelling, and warmth in the left leg
A mother 3 days post-delivery asking about postpartum lochia changes
A mother 4 days post-delivery with normal breast engorgement

questions.rationale: Unilateral calf pain, swelling, and warmth are classic signs of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), a serious postpartum thromboembolic complication requiring immediate anticoagulation evaluation.

distractor_rationales.A: Mild afterpains and successful breastfeeding are normal postpartum findings.
distractor_rationales.C: Inquiring about lochia changes is routine educational inquiry.
distractor_rationales.D: Normal breast engorgement is expected during lactation onset.

questions.question_text: What physiological cardiovascular change occurs in normal pregnancy that impacts fluid and hemodynamic assessment?

choices.text: Maternal blood volume increases by 30-50% to accommodate placental and fetal perfusion
Maternal cardiac output decreases by 80% throughout gestation
Blood pressure rises significantly to hypertensive levels in all healthy pregnant women
Total red blood cell volume decreases drastically while plasma volume remains zero

questions.rationale: Pregnancy induces marked hypervolemia (30-50% increase in plasma and blood volume) to meet metabolic and placental perfusion demands.

distractor_rationales.B: Cardiac output increases, not decreases, during normal pregnancy.
distractor_rationales.C: Blood pressure normally dips slightly in mid-pregnancy rather than rising to hypertensive levels.
distractor_rationales.D: Plasma volume increases more than red blood cell volume, causing physiological hemodilution.

questions.question_text: What is the primary post-repair instruction a midwife should give to a postnatal mother regarding episiotomy wound care at home?

choices.text: Keep the perineum strictly moist by applying occlusive plastic wraps
Keep the perineal area clean and dry, perform regular hand hygiene, practice proper front-to-back wiping, and take prescribed Sitz baths
Avoid all personal hygiene and bathing for 6 weeks
Apply harsh chemical bleaching agents to sterilize the scar

questions.rationale: Maintaining perineal cleanliness, proper front-to-back wiping, and Sitz baths promote comfort and prevent wound infection.

distractor_rationales.A: Moist plastic wraps promote bacterial growth and wound infection.
distractor_rationales.C: Avoiding personal hygiene increases infection risks.
distractor_rationales.D: Harsh chemical bleaches cause severe chemical burns and tissue necrosis.
